activities.topic: Introduction to IoT and Smart Systems

activity_1.title: Find Automatic Systems Around You
steps: Look around your house, school, farm, or village.
Find three systems that work automatically or give signals.
Observe what each system does.
examples: Water tank motor that stops when the tank fills
Street lights that turn ON in the evening

activity_2.title: Observe the Three Steps
steps: Choose one automatic system.
Identify what it detects (light, water level, movement, temperature).
Understand what decision is made.
Observe what action happens as a result.
examples: Street light: Detect → darkness, Decision → it is night, Action → light turns ON

extra_exploration.task: Find two more automatic systems in your village or farm.
examples: Irrigation pump starting when soil is dry
Solar street lights turning ON at night

think_and_notice: Which automatic system did you observe?
What signal made the system start working?
How does this system help people in daily life?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your observations with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Recognize smart systems in daily life
learning_outcomes.description: Students identify devices that work automatically using sensors or signals.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand the Sense–Think–Act process
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how systems detect information and perform actions.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop observation and analytical skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students analyze how technology solves everyday problems.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect IoT concepts with real-world applications
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand how connected devices improve efficiency and convenience.

bonus_activity: Ask someone which machine or device in your village works automatically and saves time.
Examples include irrigation motor, solar street light, and water tank alarm.
Think about how these devices make daily work easier.

activity_1.title: Observe a Human System
steps: Ask a family member to clap their hands.
Listen carefully to the sound.
Raise your hand after hearing the clap.
Observe how your body responded to the sound.

activity_2.title: Find Similar Systems Around You
steps: Look around your home or village.
Find two machines where different parts work together.
Identify the input part (receives information).
Identify the thinking part (makes decisions).
Identify the action part (performs the work).
examples: Torch: Input → switch pressed, Decision → electricity flows, Action → light turns ON

extra_exploration.task: Find three objects with buttons or switches.

think_and_notice: What part of your body heard the clap sound?
What part decided to raise your hand?
What part actually moved?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your observations with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand systems made of different parts
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe that every system has components with different roles.

learning_outcomes.title: Recognize input–processing–output concept
learning_outcomes.description: Students relate body systems and machines to the IoT process.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop observation and analytical skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students analyze how actions occur step by step.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect IoT concepts with real-life systems
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand how sensors, controllers, and devices work together.

bonus_activity: Ask which machine in your house or farm has the most buttons or controls.
Examples include tractor controls, mobile phone, and TV remote.
Think about what each button controls.

activities.topic: Understanding Control Systems and Input–Output Actions

activity_1.title: Find a Button That Controls Something
steps: Look around your house and find three devices that work when a button is pressed.
Press each button carefully.
Observe what happens after pressing it.

activity_2.title: Create Your Own Button System
steps: Choose one person to act as the button.
Choose another person to act as the machine.
Say 'Press' to trigger an action.
Say 'Release' to stop the action.
Observe how one signal controls behavior.

extra_exploration.task: Find two machines where pressing something starts an action.

think_and_notice: What happened when you pressed the button?
Did the machine start or stop after pressing it?
Why do machines use buttons or switches to control actions?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your observations with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand input and output systems
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how pressing a button (input) causes an action (output).

learning_outcomes.title: Identify control mechanisms in daily life
learning_outcomes.description: Students recognize how switches and buttons control machines.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop observation and analytical skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students analyze cause-and-effect relationships.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect IoT concepts with real-world devices
learning_outcomes.description: Students relate simple controls to how electronic systems operate.

bonus_activity: Find five buttons or switches in your house.
Examples include torch switch, fan switch, doorbell, TV remote, and mobile phone buttons.
Think about what action each button controls.

activities.topic: Understanding Alert Systems and Sound-Based Notifications

activity_1.title: Find Sound Alerts Around You
steps: Look around your home, school, or village.
Find three things that make sound to give information or warning.
Listen carefully and observe when and why the sound is produced.

activity_2.title: Create Your Own Alert System
steps: Choose one person to act as the button.
Choose another person to act as the alarm.
Say 'Start' to trigger a sound.
Say 'Stop' to stop the sound.
Observe how one signal controls an alert.
examples: Start → person makes a beep or clap sound

extra_exploration.task: Find two machines that give sound signals.

think_and_notice: Which device produced the loudest sound?
Why do machines use sound alerts instead of only lights?
How does sound help people react quickly?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your observations with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Recognize sound alert systems in daily life
learning_outcomes.description: Students identify devices that use sound to communicate information.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand warning and notification systems
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how sound signals help people notice important events.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop observation and reasoning skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students analyze when and why sound alerts are used.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect IoT concepts with real-world applications
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand how IoT devices use sound alerts for safety and notifications.

bonus_activity: Ask which machine uses sound to warn people.
Examples include pressure cooker whistle, vehicle horn, and school bell.
Think about why the sound must be loud enough for everyone to hear.

activity_1.title: Estimate Distance
steps: Choose two objects around your house.
Stand near one object.
Estimate how far the second object is.
Walk the steps to check your estimate.
examples: Example: Door to table is about 2 steps away

activity_2.title: Measure Using Steps
steps: Pick an object in your house or yard.
Stand at a distance from it.
Walk slowly towards it while counting your steps.
Observe how the distance reduces as you move closer.

extra_exploration.task: Find machines or systems that show measurements or information.

think_and_notice: Was your distance guess correct or different?
How did counting steps help you measure distance?
Why do machines sometimes need sensors to measure distance automatically?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your observations with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand distance estimation
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how distance can be estimated and measured.

learning_outcomes.title: Recognize sensing systems in technology
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand how sensors help machines detect objects.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop observation and analytical skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students analyze how distance changes with movement.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect IoT concepts with real-world systems
learning_outcomes.description: Students relate sensor technology to everyday devices.

bonus_activity: Stand at one point and identify objects that are near, medium, and far.
Examples: near → chair, medium → door, far → tree.
Think about how a machine or sensor could measure these distances automatically.

activity_1.title: Light and Darkness Observation
steps: Choose a place inside or outside your home.
Observe the brightness at two different times of the day.
Compare the light levels in the morning and evening.
Write down where it was brightest and darkest.

activity_2.title: Feel the Temperature
steps: Place your hand in different locations.
Compare temperature in each place.
Identify which place feels hotter or cooler.

extra_exploration.task: Ask about weather conditions during different times of the day.
examples: When does the air feel humid or sticky?

think_and_notice: Which place had the most light?
Which place felt cooler or warmer?
Why do machines need sensors to measure light and temperature automatically?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your observations with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand environmental changes
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe variations in light and temperature in their surroundings.

learning_outcomes.title: Recognize the role of sensors in technology
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand how sensors detect environmental conditions.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop observation and analytical skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students analyze how environmental conditions change over time.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect IoT concepts with real-world systems
learning_outcomes.description: Students relate sensors to smart devices like automatic lights and weather monitors.

bonus_activity: Find systems that react to environmental changes.
Examples include street lights turning ON at night, solar lights charging in sunlight, and fans used when temperature increases.
Think about how sensors help these systems work automatically.

activity_1.title: Control Something From Far
steps: Take help from a family member or friend.
Stand a few steps away from them.
Give a simple command like 'Start' to make them clap.
Give another command like 'Stop' to make them stop clapping.
Observe how your command from a distance controls their action.

activity_2.title: Observe Moving Machines
steps: Look around your house or village.
Find at least two machines that create movement.
Observe which part of the machine rotates or moves.
Think about how movement helps the machine perform its function.

extra_exploration.task: Ask someone at home about machines that work at a fixed time and observe how time controls their operation.
examples: School bell ringing at a certain time
Irrigation motor turning ON at a fixed hour

think_and_notice: What happened when you gave a command from far away?
Which machines around you create movement?
Why do some machines work at a fixed time?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your observations with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand remote control systems
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how commands can control actions from a distance.

learning_outcomes.title: Recognize machines that create movement
learning_outcomes.description: Students identify rotating or moving parts in everyday machines.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand time-based automation
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how machines can operate at scheduled times.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect IoT concepts with real-world systems
learning_outcomes.description: Students relate remote control and automation concepts with daily technology.

bonus_activity: Look around your house or village and find three things that can be controlled without touching them directly.
Examples include TV remote, mobile phone controlling music, and wireless speakers.
Think about how wireless technology allows devices to communicate.

activities.topic: Time-Based Systems, Non-Contact Sensing, and Information Display

activity_1.title: Observe Time-Based Activities
steps: Look around your house or village.
Find at least two activities that happen at a fixed time every day.
Observe when these activities usually occur.
Write down the time for each activity.
Think about why these activities follow a fixed schedule.
examples: Temple bell at a certain time
Irrigation motor starting at a fixed time

activity_2.title: Detect Without Touching
steps: Ask a family member to hold a small object like a stone or paper.
Stand a little distance away from the object.
Slowly bring your hand closer to the object without touching it.
Observe how you can sense the presence of the object before touching it.
Relate this observation to how sensors detect objects without contact.
examples: Feeling the presence of an object before touching it
Noticing changes in space when your hand comes closer to an object

extra_exploration.task: Look around your house and find devices where information is displayed and observe how they present information clearly.
examples: Digital clock on a mobile phone

think_and_notice: Which activity in your village happens at the same time every day?
How do people know the correct time?
Why do machines sometimes need to detect objects without touching them?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your ideas with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand time-based systems
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe activities that occur at scheduled times.

learning_outcomes.title: Recognize sensing without contact
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand that sensors can detect objects without touching them.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop observation and analytical skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students analyze how information is displayed and used in daily life.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect IoT concepts with real-world systems
learning_outcomes.description: Students relate sensors, clocks, and displays to smart systems.

bonus_activity: Look around your house and find three places where information is stored or recorded.
Examples include notebook, mobile phone memory, and calendar.
Think about why storing information is important for machines and people.

activity_1.title: Observe Access Systems
steps: Look around your house, school, or village.
Find at least two places where permission is needed before entering or using something.
Observe how access is controlled in these places.
Notice how the system checks whether a person is allowed or not.
Think about why such systems are important for safety.
examples: School gate requiring permission to enter

activity_2.title: Controlled Movement
steps: Take a door or gate in your house.
Open the door slowly.
Stop the door at different positions such as slightly open, half open, and fully open.
Observe how the door can move and stop at specific positions.
Relate this to how machines control movement precisely.

extra_exploration.task: Ask someone at home about places where identification is required and observe how systems recognize people quickly.
examples: School ID cards used for identification

think_and_notice: Why do some places require identification before entry?
How do locks or keys protect important places?
Why do machines sometimes need precise movement?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your observations with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand identification systems

learning_outcomes.title: Recognize controlled movement mechanisms
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how objects move and stop at specific positions.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop observation and reasoning skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students analyze how systems ensure safety and control.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect IoT concepts with real-world systems
learning_outcomes.description: Students relate identification and controlled movement concepts to everyday security and automation systems.

bonus_activity: Ask someone in your house where cards or IDs are used to identify people.
Examples include school ID cards, bank ATM cards, and SIM cards in mobile phones.
Think about how machines recognize these cards automatically.

activity_1.title: Observe Warning Signals
steps: Look around your house or village.
Find at least three things that give a warning signal using light or sound.
Observe when these signals are used.
Think about why these warning signals are important.
Notice how people react when they hear or see these signals.
examples: Vehicle horn used on the road
Torch light used as a signal at night

activity_2.title: Check Space Around Objects
steps: Find a place near your house where objects are kept or parked.
Observe whether the space is empty or occupied.
Notice how objects are arranged to avoid collision.
Think about how people decide where to place objects safely.
Relate this observation to how machines detect space availability.
examples: Farm tools kept near a wall

extra_exploration.task: Ask someone at home about situations where warning sounds are important and observe how alerts help people react quickly.

think_and_notice: Why do vehicles use horns or sirens?
Why is it important to warn people quickly during emergencies?
How can machines help detect whether a space is empty or full?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your observations with your parents or elders.

bonus_activity: Stand near your house and observe the road for 10 minutes.
Identify three types of signals used by vehicles such as horn sound, indicator lights, and brake lights.
Think about how these signals help prevent accidents.

activity_1.title: Find Smart or Automatic Systems
steps: Look around your house, school, or village.
Find at least three devices that work automatically or with technology.
Observe how these devices help people perform tasks easily.
Think about what makes these devices smart or automatic.
Notice how these devices reduce human effort.

activity_2.title: Observe Wireless Control
steps: Find a device that can be controlled without touching it directly.
Use or observe how the device is controlled.
Notice how commands are sent from one device to another.
Observe how quickly the device responds to the command.
Relate this to wireless communication between devices.

extra_exploration.task: Ask someone in your house which devices work using the internet or mobile phone and observe how these devices connect people and machines.

think_and_notice: Which device in your house works without many wires?
How does a remote control send commands to a device?
Why do modern machines use wireless communication?

learning_outcomes.title: Understand the concept of controllers

activities.topic: Motion Detection and Touchless Safety Systems

activity_1.title: Observe Movement Detection
steps: Stand in one place in your house or yard.
Ask a family member to walk slowly in front of you.
Observe how you notice their movement immediately.
Think about how machines can detect movement using sensors.
Relate this observation to real-life places where movement detection is useful.

activity_2.title: Touchless Signal Experiment
steps: Stand near a door or entrance.
Slowly bring your hand closer to the door area without touching it.
Imagine a system where a doorbell rings automatically when someone comes near.
Think about how this system can be useful in different places.
Relate this to touchless technology used in smart systems.

extra_exploration.task: Look around your house or village and find situations where warning signals are useful and observe how alerts help people react quickly.

think_and_notice: How do you notice when someone enters a room?
Why are touchless systems useful in public places?
Why do machines need warning signals when objects come too close?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your observations with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Understand motion detection systems
learning_outcomes.description: Students observe how movement can trigger alerts.

learning_outcomes.title: Recognize touchless technology
learning_outcomes.description: Students understand how systems can work without physical contact.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop observation and analytical skills
learning_outcomes.description: Students analyze how machines detect objects and respond.

learning_outcomes.title: Connect IoT concepts with real-world applications
learning_outcomes.description: Students relate sensor-based automation to security and safety systems.

bonus_activity: Look around your house or village and identify three situations where machines could help improve safety.
Examples include automatic light near house entrance, alarm when animals enter farm, and warning system when vehicles come close.
Think about how sensors and controllers could help build these systems.

activity_1.title: Observe Safety Signals
steps: Look around your house or village.
Find at least two situations where warning signals are used for safety.
Observe how these warnings help people notice danger quickly.
Think about why warning signals are important in daily life.
Relate this to how machines can detect and warn about danger.
examples: Smell of gas in the kitchen

activity_2.title: Observe Temperature Around You
steps: Stand in two different places such as inside the house and outside.
Feel the temperature in each place.
Observe which place feels cooler and which feels warmer.
Think about why temperature changes in different locations.
Relate this to how machines can measure temperature automatically.

activity_3.title: Observe Soil and Water in Plants
steps: Find a plant near your house or farm.
Touch the soil carefully.
Observe whether the soil is dry or wet.
Ask someone when the plant should be watered.
Think about how machines could help in watering plants automatically.

extra_exploration.task: Look around your village or farm and find situations where sensors could help farmers and think about how technology can improve decision-making.
examples: Detecting smoke or fire in fields

think_and_notice: How do people know when gas is leaking or something is burning?
Why is it important to monitor temperature in houses or farms?
How can farmers know when plants need water?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your observations with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.title: Develop observation and analytical skills

activity_1.title: Test Your Reaction Time
steps: Ask a family member or friend to hold a small object like a coin or stone.
Ask them to drop the object suddenly.
Try to catch the object as quickly as possible.
Repeat this activity three times.
Observe how quickly you react to an unexpected event.

activity_2.title: Observe Automatic Lights
steps: Look around your house or village.
Find places where lights are turned ON only when needed.
Observe when these lights are used.
Think about how these lights could work automatically.
Relate this to how sensors can control lights based on conditions.
examples: Street light turning ON at night
Torch used when it becomes dark

activity_3.title: Observe Security Signals
steps: Look around your home or village.
Find at least two systems that help protect people or property.
Observe how these systems warn people or provide security.
Think about why these systems are important.
Relate this to how machines can provide automated security.
examples: Dog barking when someone comes near

extra_exploration.task: Ask someone how they know when someone comes near the house at night and think about how sensors could detect movement automatically.

think_and_notice: How quickly were you able to react to the falling object?
Why are automatic lights useful at night?
Why are security systems important for homes and villages?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your observations with your parents or elders.

activities.topic: Touch-Free Automation and Multi-Sensor Safety Systems

activity_1.title: Observe Touch-Free Actions
steps: Look around your home or school.
Find at least two situations where people avoid touching objects directly.
Observe how people perform these actions safely.
Think about why avoiding touch is important in some situations.
Relate this to how machines can provide touch-free solutions.
examples: Using a cloth or stick to open a gate

activity_2.title: Observe Safety Signals
steps: Look around your house or village.
Identify situations where warning signals indicate danger.
Observe how people react to these signals.
Think about why quick response to these signals is important.
Relate this to how machines can detect and alert people.
examples: Smell of gas in the kitchen
Horn of a tractor or vehicle

activity_3.title: Observe Multiple Signs of Danger
steps: Think of a situation where more than one sign indicates danger.
Observe how different signals appear together.
Notice how multiple signals help identify danger faster.
Think about how combining signals improves safety.
Relate this to how multiple sensors work together in smart systems.
examples: Smell of gas and sound of leakage

extra_exploration.task: Look around your house or farm and identify places where sensors could improve safety or convenience.
examples: Sensor system for farm animals entering fields

think_and_notice: Why are touch-free systems useful in public places?
Why is it important to detect gas leaks or unusual movement quickly?
How can multiple sensors improve safety systems?
activities.discussion_instruction: Discuss your ideas with your parents or elders.

learning_outcomes.description: Students analyze how different signals indicate potential danger.
